honestCall: This reconciliation pass is real and substantive, not cosmetic: FIND-401 (OQ7 propagation into C1), FIND-403 (Smart Turn JA citation symmetry), and FIND-404 (OQ8 deploy-blocking gate) are all genuinely, verifiably fixed with matching text on both sides of every cross-reference checked — a grep sweep for 'either (a)', stale edge-tts/edge_tts/msedge-tts/energyVAD/genId/node---test references, and every OQ's resolution status confirms zero NEW contradictions were introduced and the specific defects named are gone. The Pipecat architecture itself is not re-litigated here and remains sound. However, FIND-402 was only half-fixed: the LATENCY bullet's tense claim ('verified' -> 'MEASURED... not assumed') was corrected, but the second, explicitly-named half of the same finding -- OQ8's own entry still opening with the literal word 'OPEN' directly under a section header that promises every entry is 'RESOLVED in-spec' -- was left byte-identical to the text iteration-9 already quoted as unresolved. This is the single remaining internal inconsistency in the document, it is real (not invented), it is evidenced at file:line, and neither of FIND-402's own two offered remediation paths was applied to close it. The fix is a one-line reword (see FIND-501's suggested text) that does not touch the actual decision procedure or the §4 gate that already exists — this is not a re-litigation of any architectural decision, it is the document's own stated invariant ('RESOLVED in-spec (F7)') being violated by one leftover word.
